hint1.en: Think about what they actually need, not what looks nicest.
hint1.ar: فَكِّرْ فِيمَا يَحْتَاجُونَهُ حَقًّا، لَا فِيمَا يَبْدُو أَجْمَل.

hint2.en: One of these two would really help them.

model.en: This one. Look why, then choose it yourself.
model.ar: هَذَا. اُنْظُرْ لِمَاذَا، ثُمَّ اخْتَرْهُ بِنَفْسِك.

success.en: You noticed what three grown-ups walked straight past.
success.ar: اِنْتَبَهْتَ لِمَا مَرَّ بِهِ ثَلَاثَةُ كِبَارٍ دُونَ أَنْ يَرَوْه.

payload._comment: The social beat, and deliberately built out of the same produce as everything else rather than out of a special set of 'kindness' objects. Helping somebody in a market means noticing what they actually need and knowing enough about the things on the stall to pick it — which is practical reasoning, not a separate moral subject bolted on.
payload._nofailComment: Errorless, like every other activity: a wrong pick here gets a gentler question and another go, never a face pulling a sad expression. A no-fail rule that had an exception for the kindness question would be teaching exactly the wrong thing about kindness.

prompt.en: The smallest one is thirsty, and there is no water yet. Which is full of juice?
prompt.ar: الصَّغِيرُ عَطْشَان، وَلَا مَاءَ بَعْد. أَيُّهَا مَلِيءٌ بِالعَصِير؟

revealLine.en: Watermelon is nearly all water. He drank half of it.
revealLine.ar: البِطِّيخُ كُلُّهُ مَاءٌ تَقْرِيبًا. شَرِبَ نِصْفَهُ.

prompt.en: Grandma asked for something soft she can eat without her teeth.
prompt.ar: طَلَبَتِ الجَدَّةُ شَيْئًا لَيِّنًا تَأْكُلُهُ بِلَا أَسْنَان.

revealLine.en: A banana. She did not even have to ask twice.
revealLine.ar: مَوْزَة. وَلَمْ تَحْتَجْ حَتَّى أَنْ تَطْلُبَ مَرَّتَيْن.

prompt.en: This one is already carrying too much. Which is the lightest to hand them?
prompt.ar: هَذِهِ تَحْمِلُ الكَثِيرَ بِالفِعْل. أَيُّهَا أَخَفُّ لِتُنَاوِلَهَا إِيَّاه؟

revealLine.en: The apple. You remembered what the scale showed you.
revealLine.ar: التُّفَّاحَة. تَذَكَّرْتَ مَا أَرَاكَ إِيَّاهُ المِيزَان.
